title: Klay Thompson objects to being used in Kevin Durant’s Warriors-76ers comparison
content:
When Kevin Durant originally compared LeBron James’ move to the Philadelphia 76ers to some of the biggest decisions of his own career, he didn’t mention any names. He simply remarked that when he joined a team with multiple 20-point scorers, it was labeled “unfair.”

As the story has evolved, however, Durant has identified former Golden State Warriors teammates by name on social media to defend his past decision. That hasn’t gone over well with at least one of them.

After Durant said he thought that James’ new team is more stacked individually than those Warriors, Klay Thompson, now with the Dallas Mavericks, took exception to his name being used to bolster Durant’s argument. He reposted a Bleacher Report graphic featuring Durant’s comment to his Instagram story.

“Aye man u good?” Thompson wrote, tagging Durant. “What u using my full government for?”

Durant used Thompson’s status then as supporting evidence for his point.

“Ain’t close,” Durant wrote in reply to an Instagram comment comparing the talent level of the newly formed 76ers with the 2016-17 Warriors team he left Oklahoma City to join. “Joel [Embiid] MVP, recently. Jaylen Brown, recent Finals MVP, Tyrese Maxey, All-Star in the last 3 years. We all know what Bron does.

“Klay Thompson never an MVP candidate in nothing, 22 (points per game).”

It is the latest example of Durant seemingly using James’ decision to form a superteam in Philadelphia in pursuit of another championship to validate his own much-criticized move to the 73-win Warriors after Golden State eliminated his Thunder in the previous Western Conference finals.

A reporter asked Durant for his thoughts on James choosing the 76ers on Saturday at a USA Basketball Foundation charity event. The 37-year-old said he was happy for his longtime superstar counterpart, adding, “It’s a great decision for him to go to a team that got a good chance to win. Philly, a great fan base, great market.”

He was then asked whether he believed the 76ers were legitimate contenders.

“For sure,” Durant responded. “You don’t think so? Last time they put three 20-point scorers on a team, they said it was unfair, which was the team I was on. [The 76ers] have got four 25-point scorers on this team. So, hell yeah, I think they’re going to be a contender.

“They’re going to be a fun team to watch. … I can’t wait to see it.”

At the time, Durant never explicitly identified “the team I was on” as the Warriors, but his move to Golden State in the summer of 2016 remains the prime example. Durant was vilified for leaving Oklahoma City at the peak of his powers to join the ascendant dynasty in the Bay Area alongside two-time reigning MVP Stephen Curry, Thompson and Draymond Green.

Durant also played alongside two other 20-point scorers in Brooklyn. He signed with the Nets in 2019 alongside Kyrie Irving but missed the entire 2019-20 season while recovering from the Achilles tear he suffered in the 2019 finals with Golden State against the Toronto Raptors. Brooklyn later acquired James Harden in January 2021, though the trio played only 16 games together.

Durant has now doubled down on defending his Warriors decision. At the time, he brought his 28.2 points per game from the previous season to a roster that already featured Curry averaging 30.1 and Thompson 22.1 in 2015-16. Alongside Green, who won Defensive Player of the Year in 2016-17, the group reached three straight finals and won the first two, both against James and the Cleveland Cavaliers.

In Durant’s eyes, that still pales in comparison to James joining a 76ers roster that already features three elite scorers and All-NBA talents.

“Draymond (Green), 14 (points per game), 7 rebounds, 6 assist, Steph (Curry) a MVP just like Joel (Embiid) was (in 2023),” Durant finished his Instagram comment by writing. “I don’t get how the Warriors team is better on paper.”

Thompson, however, would rather be just left out of the comparison.
